extracted.intended_audience: peer reviewers and panellists asked to review EPSRC / UKRI research grant proposals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for researchers acting as external reviewers or panellists assessing EPSRC (UKRI) research grant proposals, covering confidentiality, assessment practice, timescales and feedback procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number and selection of reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: When we receive a research proposal, we send a copy to at least three reviewers, including at least one nominated by the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The process is mainly electronic and carried out through the UKRI Funding Service. Reviewers complete their comments and return them to UK Research and Innovation Grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposal has been received by UK Research and Innovation Grants 'in confidence'. Reviewers are asked to treat the application in the same way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: UKRI and the councils undertake not to distribute the proposal to third parties other than to reach a decision on whether to fund it; reviewers should not disclose application contents outside of the decision process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on using generative AI in peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers and panellists are not permitted to use generative AI tools to develop their assessment, including to correct language, spelling, grammar and formatting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using these tools can potentially compromise the confidentiality of the ideas that applicants have entrusted to UKRI to safeguard. For more detail see our policy on the use of generative AI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymity of reviewers (to applicants) and identity in meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: To maintain anonymity when the reviewers’ comments are passed back to applicants, reviewers’ names do not appear on the form - only a reviewer reference number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reviewer reference number links the reviewer to the proposal and is unique to that application (so if a reviewer receives more than one proposal, each will have a different reference number). However, all reviewers’ comments received in time will be seen at the peer review meetings with the reviewers’ names included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review timescales
rubrics_metrics.description: Our timescales allow three weeks for sending proposals to reviewers and receiving their comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All reviewers’ comments received in time will be seen at the peer review meetings (at which reviewers' names are included).

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use journal-based metrics (DORA compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: You should not use journal-based metrics, such as journal impact factors, as a surrogate measure of the quality of individual research articles, to assess an investigator’s contributions, or to make funding decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: UKRI is committed to the San Francisco Declaration on Research Assessment (DORA). Do not rely on journal impact factor, any hierarchy of journals, conference rankings, or metrics such as the H-index or i10-index when assessing UKRI grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider broad range of research outputs and qualitative impact
rubrics_metrics.description: For the purpose of research assessment, please consider the value and impact of all research outputs (including datasets, software, inventions, patents, preprints, and other commercial activities) in addition to research publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider a broad range of impact measures including qualitative indicators of research impact, such as influence on policy and practice. The content of a paper is more important than publication metrics or the identity of the journal, especially for early-stage investigators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feedback for proposals not forwarded to a funding meeting
rubrics_metrics.description: For proposals that do not receive sufficiently strong support to be put forward to a funding meeting, investigators will be notified and the reviewers’ reports will be posted to the applicant and the applicant’s higher education institution’s research office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should be aware their reports may be shared with the applicant and institutional research office when proposals are not put forward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria and process for prioritisation and applicant response
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals that receive highly supportive comments from at least two reviewers are submitted to funding prioritisation meetings. The reviewers’ reports are passed back to the investigator to comment on any factual inaccuracies or questions raised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The investigator then has 14 days to respond to the reviewers’ comments. Any response is submitted in confidence to the meeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feedback for proposals considered at prioritisation without postal peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: All proposals considered at a prioritisation meeting that have not had a postal peer review stage will receive written comments as feedback from the meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should note that such proposals will receive written meeting feedback rather than postal peer review reports.
